data.name: Dihydromyricetin

identifiers_status.reason: Gene and protein identifiers do not apply to the type "Drug".

data.description: Flavonoid from Ampelopsis grossedentata reported to reduce fibrosis with accompanying suppression of PI3K/AKT/mTOR signalling.

page_status.reason: By design: fewer than three linked studies and not a node on the pathway map, so no page is generated. The record is still served here and in the bulk exports.

data.description_beginner: A flavonoid from vine tea. In animal studies it reduces fibrosis - the stiff scarring that replaces healthy tissue - and this comes together with a quieting of PI3K/AKT/mTOR signalling.

studies.title: Dihydromyricetin attenuates fibrosis-associated features of hypertrophic scar with accompanying changes in PI3K/AKT/mTOR-related signaling.
studies.authors: Cao P; Shi A; Wang Y; Hui S; Lyu G

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Rabbit ear hypertrophic scar model; human hypertrophic scar fibroblasts
studies.finding: Dihydromyricetin reduced collagen I/III and α-SMA in hypertrophic scar fibroblasts and improved scar elevation in a rabbit ear model, with accompanying reductions in AKT and mTOR phosphorylation; causality was not established.
